acceptanceCriteria: docs/LANE-ORCHESTRATION.md (or the lane charter template it owns) forbids `git stash` in lane worktrees and names the patch-file alternative (git diff > p.patch; git apply -R; git apply)
Optionally, the lane-ops tooling detects stash entries created from a lane worktree and reports them
body: On 2026-10-21 the dogfood-flow lane (worktree /private/tmp/cem10-build/batch-dogfood-flow) ran `git stash` / `git stash pop` for a without-fix run, while the affected-selection lane, another worktree of the same clone, had also stashed. The pop applied the affected-selection lane's stash 723eec1 instead of its own. No work was lost, because that stash matched commit dca93014a, but a lane can silently take or drop a peer's uncommitted work. Refs under refs/stash are per repository, not per worktree. The orchestrator has since added a no-stash rule to its scratch lane charter. The repository's lane guidance does not have that rule yet.

title: Lane orchestration: `git stash` is shared by every worktree of a clone, so one lane can pop another lane's stash
